label: Wool
description: Wool in furniture: Warm, springy and naturally textured, with good recovery under foot and hand.
intro: Wool appears across 2 product families and 4 options, especially on Rugs.
chemistry: Wool is a protein fibre with natural crimp, which helps it spring back and trap air. That gives wool rugs and textiles warmth, resilience and a richer tactile body than many synthetics.
It also has inherent flame resistance and good soil-hiding texture, though the fibre can felt or shrink if treated harshly with heat, agitation and moisture.
furnitureUse: In furniture contexts wool is especially strong in rugs and premium upholstery blends where thermal comfort, resilience and a natural matte finish matter.
Its trade-off is care sensitivity and price. It feels elevated, but it usually asks for a more considered maintenance routine than mass-market synthetics.
care: Moisture and wear note: Can absorb moisture vapour without feeling wet, but still needs proper drying after spills.
Care note: Vacuum gently, keep moth risk in mind in storage and use fibre-appropriate spot cleaning.
